subject: MAT
label: Grade 05
task: Meet the outcome of every unit in Grade 05 Mathematics, and keep one piece of evidence for each.
condition: A 36-week school year, 10 units, a teacher or guide, a learning book or device, and local examples in the local language first with English support.
standard: Each unit: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school. Course pass: no unit at 'Not yet' after one retry, and a pass in SA1 and SA2.

modules.title: Numbers to 10 lakh and millions
modules.outcome: read, write, compare and round large numbers
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Numbers to 10 lakh and millions', taught in a way that is short, playful, with objects, pictures and talk. The target is clear: read, write, compare and round large numbers. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Show it with objects or a picture: build or draw the idea in 'Numbers to 10 lakh and millions' before using symbols.
Say the rule in your own words, then write one worked line, naming each step.
Use it: read, write, compare and round large numbers. Start with one easy question, then one with a real-life story.
Check it: use a second method, estimate, or work backwards to test your answer.
modules.example: Model run for 'Numbers to 10 lakh and millions'. Read the question and underline what is asked. Draw or write what is known. Choose the method named in the unit. Work it line by line, one idea per line, with units where they apply. Estimate first so the answer can be tested for sense. Check by working backwards. What a good answer looks like: correct method, every step visible, units stated, and a one-line check.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Read, write, compare and round large numbers: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.

Which action verb starts the outcome of Unit 1 (Numbers to 10 lakh and millions), and at which Bloom level is it?
'read,', at the Apply level.
When do the formative checks FA1 to FA4 and the summative checks SA1 and SA2 happen?
FA1 to FA4 around weeks 6, 12, 24 and 30; SA1 in week 18; SA2 in week 36.
In which weeks does Unit 10 (Algebra beginnings) run?
Weeks 36 to 36.
What evidence do you keep for each unit, and why?
One page in your learning book. It shows what you can really do and lets a teacher check it against the standard.
ladder: L1: count, add and subtract small numbers; name shapes.
L2: use the four operations, fractions and simple measures.
L3: work with ratio, algebra beginnings and geometry reasoning.
L4: algebra, geometry proof, trigonometry and statistics.
L5: functions, calculus, vectors and probability.
L6 (degree): proof, linear algebra and modelling.
L7 (postgraduate): research mathematics, data science or teaching at depth.
